raw_segments.text: I had turned to the wilderness really, not to Mr. Kurtz, who, I was ready to admit, was
as good as buried, and for a moment it seemed to me as if I also were buried in a vast grave
I felt an intolerable weight oppressing my breast, the smell of the damp earth, the unseen
presence of victorious corruption, the darkness of an impenetrable night.
The Russian tapped me on the shoulder.
I heard him mumbling and stammering something about Brother Seaman, couldn't conceal knowledge
of matters that would affect Mr. Kurtz's reputation.
For him, evidently, Mr. Kurtz was not in his grave.
I suspect that for him, Mr. Kurtz was one of the immortals.
Well, said I at last, speak out.
As it happens, I am Mr. Kurtz's friend in a way.
